AN ACT to amend the education law and the mental hygiene law, in relation to
requiring training for teachers, administrators and instructors in the area of
mental health first aid
items.lawCode: Amd §3004, Ed L; amd §7.07, Ment Hyg L
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S6628

SPONSOR: CARLUCCI
 
TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the education law and the mental
hygiene law, in relation to requiring training for teachers, administra-
tors and instructors in the area of mental health first aid

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

This legislation will require teachers, administrators, and instructors
to receive mental health first aid training.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1: Section 3004 of the education law is amended by adding a new
subdivision 7

Section 2: Section 7.07 of the mental hygiene law is amended by adding a
new subdivision (h)

Section 3: This act shall take effective immediately.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Mental illness is a growing problem within the youth of our society.
Often times, school systems are not adept to handle the growing burden
of children mental health issues. However, by giving teachers the neces-
sary training to handle the most immediate of mental health issues, we
can begin to tackle the problem from the ground up. This bill is not
meant to replace the need of school nurses or psychiatrists, but rather
provide teachers the means with which they can held their students.

According to a study by the National Alliance of Mental Illness, 20% of
youth ages 13-18 live with a mental health condition, 11% of youth have
a mood disorder,and 10% of youth have behavior or conduct disorder. Or
those students who have mental health issues, 50% drop out of high
school.

This legislation will prove a necessary step in tackling this state -
and countries - mental health crisis.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

None

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:

To be determined

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effective immediately.

summary: Requires training for teachers, administrators and instructors in the area of mental health first aid; requires office of mental health to assist in development of curriculum for training.
